holdings.thesis: HOLD: stop-loss flag deepens to -33.7% vs. cost basis (from -26.7%), but no company-specific negative catalyst found -- in fact positive product news this window (1.6T ZeroFlap Active Light Cable launch 10/12; SRMO micro-emitter optics standardization plus an AMD programmable-logic AI accelerator partnership, both 10/13). Today's broad move traces to a hot September CPI print (10yr yield toward ~5.27%) compounding a two-session chip-sector selloff from China's CXMT competing memory-chip news (10/13, hit Micron -5.8%, spread to Nvidia/AMD); Trefis (10/13) attributes CRDO's drop specifically to pre-existing customer-concentration risk and rich valuation (~42x NTM EV/EBITDA), not new news. Fundamentals remain strong (revenue growth +114.7% YoY, earnings growth +97.1% YoY). Next earnings ~Dec 1 (unconfirmed). Continuing to hold given no thesis-breaking catalyst. Position ~6.0%.

HOLD: no material new news this window. CEO von Ahn's latest Form 4 (period 10/7) shows an option exercise + sale of 110,046 shares at $150.63-153.26 under his existing 10b5-1 plan -- incremental, same pattern as prior routine sales, not an escalation. Analyst consensus remains mixed (Hold-leaning, avg target ~$114-134 across sources). Known Max-tier sunset/AI-reinvestment story and earnings-growth flag (-27.5% YoY) unchanged. Next earnings confirmed 11/9. Return +9.6% vs. cost basis. Position ~11.0%.

HOLD, watch continues: stop-loss flag deepens sharply to -33.0% (from -26.4%) with no negative company-specific catalyst found -- Yahoo's news feed for 10/9-14 shows only a new motion-capture/robotics AI lab opening (positive) and generic peer-comparison listicles. CFO transition (Jayant Chauhan) and reaffirmed ~40%+ FY2026 revenue growth guidance remain the operative drivers. Reads as beta amplification in today's chip-sector/CPI-driven selloff rather than fundamental deterioration. Next earnings estimated ~11/5 (unconfirmed, sources conflict with 11/19). Continuing to hold given no thesis-breaking news and a small (~1.4%) position, but flagging for very close attention next review given the pace of the decline.

HOLD, watch continues: stop-loss flag deepens to -31.1% (from -26.6%). No new VRT-specific catalyst found; the slide since the 9/8 high is attributed to valuation concerns (P/E >2x market, per Trefis 10/2) rather than a discrete event, and analyst target trims (Jefferies Buy->Hold $260 PT; Citi/KeyBanc) trace back to the July Q2 cycle, not new -- consensus remains Moderate Buy (~$357 avg target, MarketBeat 9/28). Next earnings still estimated 10/20-10/21 (company-unconfirmed). Already trimmed once (9/16); continuing to hold given no fresh thesis-breaking catalyst. Position ~7.7%.

HOLD, still slightly over the 15% position cap (~15.83%, within the 2% trim tolerance so no forced trim) -- no room to add: no new catalyst found this window beyond stale items (JPMorgan $420 PT, capex guide $195-205B, both Jul/Aug). Q3 earnings expected ~10/27-28 alongside AMZN/MSFT; heavy capex guide and the TPU/Anthropic compute-supply dynamic remain the key swing factors. Return +3.0% vs. cost basis. Position ~15.83%.

HOLD: no new catalyst found this window (nothing dated 10/13-14; most recent relevant items are from April). Riding the broad CPI/yield-driven selloff ahead of the 10/29 print. AWS growth rate and the raised ~$220B 2026 capex guide remain the key watch items into earnings. Return -2.3% vs. cost basis. Position ~12.5%.

HOLD: no fresh company-specific news found this window; the Wells Fargo relative-valuation call favoring BP is from 10/1 (stale), not new. $20B 2026 buyback program remains supportive; oil-price volatility from the 10/8 tanker-attack spike remains a near-term tailwind for XOM's integrated-energy exposure. Next earnings expected ~10/30. Return +10.7% vs. cost basis. Position ~12.5%.

HOLD: no new company-specific news found 10/13-14; Evercore's outperform/$95 PT and the Amazon contract renewal (already known) remain the core support. Return has compressed to +0.8% vs. cost basis (from +11.4%) on today's broad selloff, with fintech/rate-sensitive names hit hard; no fundamental change found to explain the move beyond the macro CPI/yield backdrop. Next earnings confirmed 11/5 (fiscal Q1 FY2027). Position ~5.9%.

HOLD: no new company-specific news found 10/13-14; Jefferies' downgrade to Hold ($280 PT) is from 7/21 (stale, valuation-driven after a 94% YTD rally at the time), not new. The ~30% FY26 revenue growth guide remains the core support. Next earnings tentatively early November (unconfirmed). Return +20.3% vs. cost basis (compressed from +26.6% on today's broad software-sector pullback). Position ~4.9%.
HOLD: no market-moving readout or company-specific news found this window; next earnings 10/29. Return +4.2% vs. cost basis. Position ~4.3%.

HOLD: no new SOFI-specific news found this window; the Muddy Waters short-report dispute (company says it's weighing legal action) remains unresolved/unescalated since Jul/Aug, not a new development. Return has widened to -16.6% vs. cost basis (from -10.6%) on today's broad rate-driven selloff hitting fintech particularly hard. Next earnings confirmed 10/27. Position ~2.6%.

HOLD: no new catalyst found this window; the John Fabick Tractor acquisition (announced 9/29) is still not confirmed closed -- an Oct 7 report repeated the same "~30 days to close" estimate, no closing confirmation found as of 10/14. Return -3.9% vs. cost basis. Position ~3.0%.

HOLD: no confirmed new company-specific catalyst this window. Goldman Sachs cut its PT to $28 from $39 on 10/7 (prior window, already somewhat priced); today's further decline reads as rate-driven (10yr toward 5.27% on the hot CPI print) layered on that cut, not a new fundamental break. One unconfirmed, conflicting report referenced softer preliminary Q3 originations -- Q3 earnings aren't until 11/3, so this is not corroborated and should not be treated as confirmed. Centerbridge Partners forward-flow deal remains the core support. Return -12.2% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.6%.

HOLD, watch continues: no new escalation found -- Berger Montague's board-fiduciary-duty inquiry remains solicitation-stage only, last restated 9/14, no deadline or court action surfaced since. FY2026 results (revenue +141% YoY, $2.7B bookings) and new P550/JUMP 20 contract wins remain supportive. Return -14.3% vs. cost basis (widened from -9.7% on today's broad defense/growth-sector pullback). Position ~1.4%.

HOLD, flagged for monitoring: stop-loss flag deepens to -28.9% (from -20.6%) with no new negative catalyst found -- RBC's downgrade to Sector Perform (10/2, stock then $57.04) is 12 days old and already priced in; no new litigation, offering, or guidance change found since beyond the known Pomerantz/Hunter and Delclaux suits. Reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance ($150-200M) stands; the lost BlueBird 7 (Blue Origin launch anomaly) keeps the ~45-satellite 2026 target at risk, already known. Reads as beta-driven selling on an already de-risked, high-beta name. Next earnings ~11/9 (estimate, unconfirmed). Return -28.9% vs. cost basis. Position ~1.4%.

HOLD: no new catalyst found this window. Correction: the previously cited "~10/27-28" next-earnings estimate traces to last year's FY2026 Q2 report date (10/28/25) -- the current cycle's date is genuinely unconfirmed, not just conservatively unconfirmed. The $4B Airedale cooling agreement and Gentherm spinoff remain the known drivers. Return -14.7% vs. cost basis (widened from -6.6% on today's broad selloff). Position ~0.5%.

HOLD: correcting a stale note -- the DZYNE acquisition is confirmed completed (~$875.8M, forming Ondas Sentinel), not still "in talks" as previously logged; 2026 revenue target has been raised to $525M+ on the back of it. Sentrycs' World Cup drone-defense selection and the 4M Defense border-clearing tender win remain known/priced drivers. Growth remains largely acquisition-driven. Return -16.9% vs. cost basis (widened from -9.2% on today's broad selloff). Position ~0.7%.

HOLD (bullish lean): no negative news found; mildly positive analyst tape referenced around 10/14 (a Street-high price-target note plus RKLB listed among that day's ARK/Cathie Wood buys, though exact figures weren't independently confirmable). Iridium deal remains on track (HSR cleared 8/12, S-4 filed, expected close mid-2027). Next earnings 11/9. Return -15.3% vs. cost basis (widened from -8.1% on today's broad selloff). Position ~1.1%.

HOLD: no new catalyst found this window; the latest confirmed item remains the 10/6 Pentagon contract disclosure (the GE Aerospace GEK800 teaming item referenced in a past review traces back to 2025 and is not new). Next earnings 10/29. Return -16.3% vs. cost basis (widened from -14.1% on today's broad defense/growth pullback). Position ~0.4%.

HOLD: no new DOJ or legal development found since the 10/13 Q3 beat (adjusted EPS $4.69 vs. $4.14 expected, revenue $112.7B, medical cost ratio improved to 88.4%, FY guidance raised to at least $20.50) -- searches surfaced only stale, already-known items (2025 DOJ Medicare Advantage probe, 2025 shareholder/defamation suits, MN provider-law suit). The quant screen's revenueGrowth(-0.4%) flag reads as a stale/trailing data-field artifact, not corroborated by any news of an actual revenue decline, and conflicts with the reported revenue beat. Return +6.6% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.7%.

HOLD: stop-loss flag deepens to -33.1% (from -26.3%) with no new negative catalyst found. One single-source, unverified report (mydailybyte.com, 10/3) claims the Merlin-01 satellite launched successfully via SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg around 10/3 with shares +8% that day -- a potential positive if corroborated, but treated cautiously given the single thin source and that it predates this window. CFO Rick Dunn's departure (~8/21) is already known/stale. Continuing to hold given the tiny (~0.2%) position size and the absence of any thesis-breaking news, though the pace of the decline warrants close attention next review. Return -33.1% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.2%.

HOLD: no new catalyst found this window; Q3 earnings date is uncertain between 10/15 (Earnings Whispers/BMO) and 10/19 (Bullstory), neither company-confirmed -- could be as early as tomorrow. Correction: the ~$210B backlog figure from the Q2 release is total company backlog, not defense-specific as previously framed; raised FY26 guidance stands. Return -1.7% vs. cost basis. Position ~0.5%.

BUY: Broadcom sourced from the standard watchlist screen (highest-ranked non-opportunity-tier, non-disqualified candidate; quant score driven by 85.5% revenue growth, 215.3% earnings growth, forward P/E 17.9). No fresh negative news found -- today's weakness reads as a normal pullback (-29.5% June-Sept per Trefis 10/6) ahead of the December fiscal Q4 print, not a new catalyst; watch the Marvell/Google custom-chip competitive narrative. Passed on the two higher-scoring opportunity-tier names on this screen: RCAT (CRO terminated 'for Cause' 7/21 with an unresolved retaliation suit, plus a separate pending securities class action and continued insider selling -- still disqualified) and SERV (Uber Eats relationship now confirmed effectively ending in early 2027 per the Aug 6/7 call, with Uber having since sold its entire equity stake -- disqualification stands, if anything stronger than before) -- and on ZENA (no fresh red flag, but a persistent dilution/share-count concern, 201M shares out per its 10/2 6-K, that's a specific, research-tied reason to pass rather than second-guessing the screen on familiarity grounds). Not opportunity-tier (~$1.65T market cap); sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor ($78.03), the binding constraint today, freed primarily by today's IONQ sale.
